R&N_ITB,test_temp_R&N_ITB_chunk_379,79,6.1_Plant_Configuration,"6, 1",content,"text, list_item",6._DESIGN_AND_OPERATIONAL_REQUIREMENTS > 6.1_Plant_Configuration,Design and Operational Requirements,Plant Configuration,Combined Cycle Power Plant,,,"Combined Cycle Power Plant, dual fuel gas turbines (GTs), dry low NOx combustors, heat recovery steam generators (HRSGs), bypass stack, diverter dampers, guillotine damper (horizontal/vertical sealing), condensing steam turbine (CST), air cooled condenser, synchronous generators, generator circuit breakers (GTGs, STGs), generator step-up transformers (2-winding)",True,"Plant configuration list explicitly includes ""Condensing Steam Turbine (CST) with Air Cooled Condenser"".",True,,high,False,"Defines overall plant configuration and major equipment packages for combined cycle plant
column2: strong anchors for matching existing plant configuration, SLD, equipment lists, and system descriptions.","The Plant shall be designed as a Combined Cycle Power Plant, consisting of but not limited to:

column1: - Dual Fuel Gas Turbine (GTs)
- Dry low NOx combustors
- Heat Recovery Steam Generators (HRSGs),
- By-pass  stack  including  diverter  dampers  horizontal  and  vertical  sealing  guillotine damper.
- Condensing Steam Turbine (CST) with Air Cooled Condenser
- Synchronous Generators for Gas Turbines and Steam Turbine
- Generator Circuit Breakers for GTGs and STGs
- 2 winding Generator Step-up transformers
- 2 or 3 winding Auxiliary transformers
- HV Circuit Breakers for GSU Transformers of GTGs and STG
The plant shall be designed preferably symmetrically
column2: this means the Plant shall consist of equally designed Groups (same number and type of GTs/HRSGs/ST)."

column1: R&N_ITB,test_temp_R&N_ITB_chunk_381,"80, 81",6.2.1_Air_Cool_Condenser,"6, 2, 1",content,"text, list_item",6._DESIGN_AND_OPERATIONAL_REQUIREMENTS > 6.2_Design_Conditions_&_Requirements > 6.2.1_Air_Cool_Condenser,Design and Operational Requirements,Air Cooled Condenser,ACC performance and scope of supply,,,"air cooled condenser (ACC), condense full steam turbine exhaust (including bypass), supporting calculations, wind direction impact on ACC performance, condensate extraction pumps, vacuum raising and maintaining system, steam duct/distribution system, condenser air removal system, cooling air fans with automatic controls, performance testing tapping points, IP and LP bypass dump steam flows, N+1 fans",True,"Section titled ""6.2.1 Air Cool Condenser"" with detailed ACC scope (fans, steam duct, vacuum system, condensate pumps, performance, N+1 fans).",True,,high,False,"Contains explicit ACC functional requirements, transient scenarios, redundancy (N+1 fans), and detailed component scope—strong retrieval anchors for ACC datasheets, P&IDs, calculations, and system descriptions.","The condenser shall be capable of condensing the whole of the steam exhaust from the steam turbine (including the bypass systems) under all conditions of load and operation. For this the EPC Contractor shall provide  with  his  proposal  supporting  calculations.  Additionally,  supporting  calculations  demonstrating that the wind direction at the site will not impact the performance of the ACCs shall be provided. The ACC location shall be selected so that it will not be in the predominant wind direction.
The systems and components for the ACC shall be provided by the Contractor and shall include but not limited to the following:
- Condensate extraction pumps and strainers
- Vacuum raising and maintaining system
- Turbine blow off tank
- Condensate, air extraction, recirculation, air, drain and atmospheric exhaust pipework and valves
- Vent pipework routed to a safe location
- Flash boxes (with integral connections to condenser) for feed heater and other drains
- Heat exchange sections
- Support structure and fan deck
- Steam duct / distribution system
- Condensate collection system
- Condenser air removal system
- Cooling air fans with automatic controls
- Condenser atmospheric relief devices
- Holding down bolts, plates, etc
- Local ladders, galleries and hand railing
- All driving motors with base plates, or stools for all auxiliaries
- Local instruments, gauges, control and panels
- Additional  tapping  points,  complete  with  isolation  and  all  necessary  instruments  for performance testing
- Any special lifting tackle, spanners and tools
- All other equipment required for the safe and efficient operation of the plant.
The  exhaust  steam  from  the  Steam  Turbine  exhaust  shall  be  directed  to  the  air  cooled  condenser  and condensing  system  via  a  steam  piping  and  ductwork  system
column2: the  water  will  then  be  forwarded  to  the condensate system.

column1: The condenser and the cooling system, at a minimum, shall be capable of:
- i. Condensing the total steam flow from its associated steam turbine operating at maximum flow and at maximum ambient temperature
- ii. Accepting the total steam system drain flows
- iii. Condensing the full capability of the steam turbine bypass system(s)
- iv. simultaneously  operating  with  steam  flow  through  the  steam  turbine  and  the  steam  turbine  bypass system.
The condensing plant shall be designed and guaranteed to condense the maximum exhaust steam flow from the Steam Turbine
column2: to accept the relevant steam system drains
column3: and to condense the dump steam flows from

column1: the IP and LP bypass systems under conditions of turbine start-up, rapid load reduction, partial or full load rejection and turbine trip.
The ACC shall be provided with N+1 fans where N refers to the number of fans required for the maximum load condition. There is no requirement to provide the ACC equipped with elevator.
The condenser vacuum shall be optimised by the EPC Contractor."

R&N_ITB,test_temp_R&N_ITB_chunk_382,81,6.2.1_Air_Cool_Condenser,"6, 2, 1",content,text,6._DESIGN_AND_OPERATIONAL_REQUIREMENTS > 6.2_Design_Conditions_&_Requirements > 6.2.1_Air_Cool_Condenser,Design and Operational Requirements,Air Cooled Condenser,ACC design details and standards,,,"LP turbine exhaust to condenser transition (minimal obstructions), negligible pressure drop, turbine bypass dumps dispersion headers, ACC materials selection, demineralized water chemistry (OEM guidelines), steam ejectors or mechanical vacuum pumps, hogging duty and running duty device per condenser, steam for air ejectors from main steam supply, silencer on ejector outlet, hotwell tank sizing (HEI standards), instrumentation for condenser tube leakage troubleshooting",True,"ACC design details: LP exhaust transition to condenser, bypass dumps, ACC materials, vacuum system (hogging/holding), hotwell/condensate instrumentation.",True,,high,False,"Provides concrete ACC mechanical/process design requirements, vacuum system options, and explicit standard reference (HEI), suitable for matching condenser/vacuum system design documents and specifications.","The steam turbine outlet connection pieces shall be designed for smooth transition with minimal obstructions from the LP turbine exhaust to the condenser to assure negligible pressure drop.
The turbine bypass dumps shall be designed with dispersion headers internal to the condenser to adequately disperse the steam safely into the condenser for all possible extreme transient scenarios.

The Air-Cooled condenser materials shall be selected to provide the necessary reliability at an economical cost taking into account that ACC is being operated with Demineralized water with proper water chemistry required by OEM guidelines. ACC OEM Design will take into consideration of proper material selection as per Demin water quality..

Vacuum raising and maintaining plant may be based on either steam ejectors or mechanical vacuum pumps. As a minimum, one start-up (hogging) duty and one running duty device shall be provided for each condenser.
Steam for air ejectors, if supplied, shall be taken from the main steam supply. A silencer shall be provided on each ejector outlet.
The hotwell tank and condensate system shall be sized in accordance with HEI standards.
The condensate system shall be equipped with instrumentation that will assist in trouble shooting of any condenser tube leakage."

- Cooling tower/fin fan cooler cells : N+1
- Tanks (if not mentioned hereunder) : more than 1
- CCW Expansion Tanks : 1 x 100%
- Atmospheric drain tank : 1 x 100%
- Vacuum Flash Tank : 1 x 100%
- Condensate Storage Tank : 2x50% or 1x100%
- Service air receiver tank : 2 x 100%
- Instrument air receiver tank : 2 x 100%

- GT Fuel Gas Last Chance Filter (per GT) : 2 x 100% Chemical tanks
- DM plant : N+1 stream
- Air conditioning :  N+1  (except  for  non-plant  buildings,  such  as: Administration building/ workshop/warehouse/Gate guard house)
- Ventilation Fans :  N+1  (except  for  non-plant  buildings,  such  as: Administration building/ workshop/warehouse/Gate guard house))
- Gas reducing station : 3 x 50%
- Feed water control stations : 2 x 100%
- Fuel Gas Boosting Compressors: : N+1, where, N=Number of Gas Turbines
- Air  compressors  with  after  coolers  (after  coolers  if  required,  will  be  confirmed  during  detail engineering) : 3x50%
- Air filtering skids : 2 x 100%
- Air dryers : 2 x 100%
- After Filters : 2 x 100%
- CO2 rack & manifold station for each GT : 1 x 100%
- CO2 rack & manifold station for each ST : 1 x 100%
- N2 rack & manifold station : 1 x 100%
- H2 generator : 2 x 100%
- Drain and vent valves :  two  valves  in  series  (If  operating  pressure  is greater than 4 MPa) otherwise single valve
- Level control valve for HRSG Drums and Feedwater tank :  N+1 (not applicable for startup line, as applicable)
Provision of bypass valves for control valves shall apply for those systems/facilities which can also be reasonably controlled manually."

R&N_ITB,test_temp_R&N_ITB_chunk_720,218,10.3.2_Condensing_Steam_Turbines,"10, 3, 2",content,text,10.1_Fuel_System > 10.3.2_Condensing_Steam_Turbines,Steam Turbine Generator,Condensing Steam Turbines,Air-cooled condenser configuration,,,"water scarcity, wet cooling towers not feasible, air-cooled condensers, steam turbine exhaust, manufacturer standard design, directly coupled 60 Hz generators, located indoors, ventilated atmosphere",True,Explicitly states “air-cooled condensers will be the basis for steam turbine condensers” and mentions “air-cooled condenser configuration”.,True,,high,False,"Defines condenser cooling basis (air-cooled), generator coupling/frequency, and indoor/ventilated installation requirements—useful anchors to retrieve STG/ACC design documents.","Due to the scarcity of water, solutions involving wet cooling towers are not feasible and air-cooled. condensers  will  be  the  basis  for  steam  turbine  condensers.  The  steam  turbine  exhaust  and  air-cooled condenser  configuration  shall  be  as  per  manufacturer's  standard  design.  The  steam  turbines  shall  be complete with and directly coupled to 60Hz generators. Steam turbines shall be provided for the Plant as defined in this OTS and shall be located indoors in a ventilated atmosphere."

R&N_ITB,test_temp_R&N_ITB_chunk_721,219,10.3.2_Condensing_Steam_Turbines,,content,text,10.1_Fuel_System > 10.3.2_Condensing_Steam_Turbines,Steam Turbine Generator,Condensing Steam Turbines,Reheat multi-pressure condensing turbine requirements,,,"reheat multiple pressure condensing type, air-cooled condenser, direct coupling, two-pole generator, 60 Hz, impulse or reaction blading acceptable, HP turbine steam admission, stop and control valves, steam turbine governor, stable conditions control",True,Mentions turbine is “condensing type using an air-cooled condenser”.,True,,high,False,"Provides specific turbine type (reheat, multi-pressure, condensing) and control/valving requirements that can match STG datasheets/specifications and control narratives.","The turbine shall be a reheat, multiple pressure condensing type using an air-cooled condenser and be suitable for direct coupling to a two-pole generator for power generation at 60 Hz. Designs for impulse or reaction blading, or for combinations thereof, are equally acceptable.

The steam admission to the HP turbine section shall be via suitable stop and control valves. The steam turbine governor shall be capable of controlling the steam turbine to maintain stable conditions."

R&N_ITB,test_temp_R&N_ITB_chunk_741,224,10.4.1_Steam_Turbine_Condensers,"10, 4, 1",content,"text, list_item",10.4_Condensing_Systems > 10.4.1_Steam_Turbine_Condensers,Condensing Systems,Steam Turbine Condensers,Air Cooled Condenser (ACC) system scope,,,"air cooled condenser (ACC), steam turbine exhaust to condenser steam duct, LP-steam headers letdown, condensate collection headers, air moving system, fan drives, steel support structure (platforms, stairways, escape ladder), air recirculation prevention, noise attenuation features, earthing and lightning protection, air evacuation pumps, ejector condenser drain tank strainers, condensate tank and drain, drain and vent pumping (valves, traps), steam turbine bypass steam on trip, reserve capacity for steam turbine overloads, ACC outside heat transfer surface cleaning (semi-automatic)",True,"Explicitly titled 'Air Cooled Condenser (ACC) system scope' and lists ACC equipment (steam ducting, fan drives, steel support structure, air evacuation pumps, ACC cleaning system).",True,,high,False,"Defines ACC condenser system scope and functional sizing requirements (operating ranges, bypass on trip, reserve capacity) with multiple equipment/interface anchors useful for matching condenser/ACC datasheets, P&IDs, layouts, and electrical/control documents.","Air cooled condenser(s) will be required to let down steam from the condensing part of the steam turbine and from the LP-steam headers.
The system shall comprise at least the following equipment:
- steam duct from the steam reducing stations to condenser and steam distribution ducting,
- steam duct from turbine exhaust flange to condenser and steam distribution ducting,
- condensate collection headers,
- air moving system,
- fan drives,
- steel support structure, including maintenance platforms, access stairways and escape ladder,
- facilities for prevention of air recirculation,
- noise attenuation features/devices as required,
- all  required  electrical  and  control  equipment  for  safe  operation,  monitoring  and  measuring, earthing and lightning protection,
- air evacuation pumps, if applicable,
- ejector condenser, drain tank and strainers at ejector steam inlets,
- condensate tank and drain,
- drain and vent pumping, piping, valves and traps with supports, and
- semi-automatic ACC outside heat transfer surface cleaning system.

The steam turbine condenser shall be complete in every respect for reliable, efficient and safe operation for a high service lifetime. The design of the air-cooled condenser shall be in accordance with the ambient conditions at Project Site and steam turbine requirements.
The condenser shall be sized to receive:
- Condense all steam for all operating ranges
- Accept the full steam turbine bypass steam when the steam turbine trips.
The  capacity  of  the  steam  turbine  condenser  shall  include  a  reserve  to  cover  possible  steam  turbine overloads."

R&N_ITB,test_temp_R&N_ITB_chunk_742,"224, 225",10.4.1.1_Air_moving_system,"10, 4, 1, 1",content,text,10.4_Condensing_Systems > 10.4.1_Steam_Turbine_Condensers > 10.4.1.1_Air_moving_system,Condensing Systems,Steam Turbine Condensers,Air moving system (axial fans and drives),,,"heat exchanging cell, individual axial flow fan, adjustable fan blades (when out of service), variable speed motor drive, continuous outdoor service, cold start at any ambient temperature (specified range), shock loading from reverse rotation (wind/convection), reverse rotation lock (alternative), remote control from Control Room, optimize configuration based on ambient condition",True,Describes ACC air moving system: 'heat exchanging cell' with 'individual axial flow fan' and 'variable speed motor' remote control.,True,,high,False,"Provides specific technical requirements for ACC fan/drive design, operability, and control interfaces that can retrieve fan datasheets, motor/VSD specs, control narratives, and ACC mechanical design documents.","The cooling air to each heat exchanging cell shall be forced by individual axial flow fan
column2: each fan, whose blades shall be adjustable when the fan is out of service, shall be driven by a variable speed motor.

column1: All the components of the fan/drive unit shall be designed for continuous outdoor service over the range of air condenser loads, ambient air temperatures and air temperatures adjacent to the tube bundles.
It shall be possible to initiate a cold start of the fans during any ambient air temperature within the specified range.

All drive components shall be rated to take into account any shock loading that may occur from starting a fan which may be rotating in a reverse direction under the influence of prevailing winds or convection currents. As an alternative, a reverse rotation lock may be provided.
Each fan drive shall be individually remotely controlled from the Control Room allowing the operator to optimize the operative configuration on the basis of actual ambient condition."

R&N_ITB,test_temp_R&N_ITB_chunk_743,225,10.4.1.2_ACC_cleaning_system,"10, 4, 1, 2",content,text,10.4_Condensing_Systems > 10.4.1_Steam_Turbine_Condensers > 10.4.1.2_ACC_cleaning_system,Condensing Systems,Steam Turbine Condensers,ACC cleaning system,,,"air cooled condenser (ACC), outside heat transfer surface cleaning, semi-automatic high-pressure spray-water cleaning, periodic cleaning during normal operation, maintain heat transfer coefficient, cleaning while ACC in operation",True,Section 'ACC cleaning system' and states cleaning while 'the ACC is in operation'.,True,,high,False,"States explicit requirement for an ACC spray-water cleaning system and operational constraints, useful to match ACC auxiliary systems, water supply/cleaning system P&IDs, and O&M documentation.","It shall be possible to clean the outside heat transfer surfaces by application of well established cleaning procedures. A semi-automatic high-pressure spray-water cleaning system shall be supplied for periodically cleaning the heat exchanger external surfaces during normal operation, keeping them free of deposits and maintaining the heat transfer coefficient of the condenser. It shall be possible for this cleaning system to be used whilst the ACC is in operation."

R&N_ITB,test_temp_R&N_ITB_chunk_950,"290, 291",11.10.2_Power_Block_and_BOP_Commissioning_Tests,,content,"text, list_item",11._OWNER'S__MINIMUM__INSPECTIONS__&__TESTING__ON__FACTORY__AND__SITE__QUALITY_ACCEPTANCE_TESTS > 11.7_Turn-Over-Packages > 11.10.2_Power_Block_and_BOP_Commissioning_Tests,Owner's Minimum Inspections & Testing,Turn-Over Packages,Power Block and BOP Commissioning Tests,,,"GT OEM dual redundant electrical overspeed trip devices, mechanical overspeed trip device cannot be provided, bearing metal temperature not applied to GT trip function, bearing metal temperature high alarm only, shaft vibration high alarm and trip, overspeed trip interlock test at full speed no load (FSNL), simulation interlock test at GT shutdown condition, electric overspeed trip devices approved by SIL study, generator cooling system (hydrogen/water/air) functionality test, generator oil seal system functionality test, speed governor no load tests (start sequence, speed steps, natural oscillations, synchronization range), speed governor on load tests (load rejection at 100%, island operation, exhaust gas high temperature limiter), steam turbine EHC (electro-hydraulic control) if applicable, Air Cooled Condenser vacuum leak test, HVAC relative moisture test, HVAC air balance, overhead crane static load tests, demineralization plant pumps running tests",True,Explicit section 'Air Cooled Condenser' with commissioning requirements including 'Logic and interlock tests' and 'Vacuum leak test'.,True,,high,False,"Provides specific commissioning/test requirements and design constraints (overspeed trip redundancy, SIL study, FSNL testing) plus equipment-specific test scopes (ACC vacuum leak, EHC, HVAC, crane, demin plant) useful for MDL retrieval.","GT OEM will provide dual redundant Electrical over speed trip devices as per OEM standard design, and Mechanical over speed trip device cannot be provided.

The high bearing metal temperature will not be applied to GT trip function as per OEM standard design. The high temperature alarm will be provided. The shaft vibration (not bearing vibration) high alarm and trip functions will be provided.
Over speed Trip interlock test will be carried out after Gas turbine reaches full speed no load.
Regarding other trip tests, simulation interlock test will be carried out at Gas Turbine shut down condition.
Electric over speed tip devices shall be approved by SIL study during the execution stage.
- Gas and steam Turbine Cooling generator system (hydrogen, water or air) and oil seal generator system
